reason: Cooling the carbon-bearing wind seems like a direct way to bring carbon into the dust.

effect: The wind produced carbonaceous grains, so I can move on to mixing the stellar ejecta.
reaction: The cooling-to-grains connection was clear and satisfying.
reason: This is the only available combination and should help build the mixed cloud.

effect: The ejecta created a shock that heats and compresses surrounding gas, rather than immediately forming a mixed cloud.
reaction: The distinction was a useful surprise.
reason: This is the only available combination, so I’ll follow the shock’s evolution.

effect: The shocked gas cooled by radiating energy, producing an enriched cloud that can receive more stellar material.
reaction: The explanation made the transition from shock to cloud clearer.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it should add the wind's carbon-bearing material to the cloud.
expectation: I expect a more carbon-enriched cloud, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The wind has mixed into the cloud, setting up the addition of material from later stellar generations.

reason: This is the only available combination and should add further stellar products to the cloud.
expectation: I expect a more broadly enriched cloud, though I’m unsure which materials will appear.

reason: Cooling the mixed element supply seems a direct route toward the grain-making goal.
expectation: I expect cooling to produce solid grains, though I am unsure which kinds.

alternatives.reason: Oxygen-rich material may contribute to rock-forming grains, but cooling seems the more direct first step.

reaction: The connection between oxygen, silicon and magnesium made the next step clear.
reason: Cooling the vapor is the only available combination and should form solid silicate grains.
expectation: I expect silicate grains to condense, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: Cooling formed silicate grains, which can now be combined with the iron-bearing grains.
reaction: The progression from vapor to microscopic mineral grains was clear.

reaction: It was useful to learn that the materials can separate again if a body melts.
reason: This is the only available combination and should bring carbon into the dust.
expectation: I expect a mixed dust stock containing carbonaceous, silicate and metal grains.

effect: The carbonaceous and rock-forming grains made mixed interstellar dust, completing the remaining goal; its surfaces can help molecules form.
reaction: The reminder that dust is a small fraction of a gas-dominated cloud was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling silicate-forming vapor into grains was most worthwhile: it clearly connected mineral ingredients to the microscopic beginnings of rock.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding successive stellar contributions to the cloud felt somewhat repetitive, even though it reinforced their different origins.

surprise.text: The ejecta first drove a shock that heated and compressed gas, rather than immediately making a mixed cloud.

arbitrary.text: Using open space to turn the shock into a cooling cloud was not obvious beforehand; the result explained radiative cooling, but the pairing itself felt somewhat abstract.

continue.text: I would continue: the progression from stellar material to dust made me curious how those grains eventually become planets, although the run of only-available choices limited meaningful decisions.
